title: Tavern off the Green
venue_description:
Tavern off the Green

Tucked on Morris Street a few blocks from the Morristown Green, Tavern off the Green calls itself the town's "unfussy local watering hole" — and it plays the part well. Pool tables, dart boards, sports on every screen and a regular-heavy crowd give the room a lived-in neighborhood-bar feel that stands apart from the more polished restaurant-bars nearby.

Atmosphere and Setting

The room is casual and unpretentious: a long bar, a scatter of tables, pool and darts toward the back, and a stage area used for local bands most weekends. It is the kind of spot regulars call their own, drawn as much by the crowd and the games as by the drink list.

Live Music and the Open Jam

Music is a regular fixture here rather than an occasional special. Tavern off the Green hosts an Open Jam every other Wednesday night, with sets generally starting between 8:00 PM and 9:30 PM — the venue points patrons to its Instagram and Facebook pages to confirm the exact start time for any given date. The jam draws local musicians looking to sit in for a few songs in a low-pressure bar-room format rather than a formal showcase.

Other Events

Beyond the open jam, Tavern off the Green regularly books local and regional bands playing country, rock and covers on weekends and several weekday evenings, making it one of the more consistently live rooms in downtown Morristown. On nights without a band, pool, darts and sports on TV keep the room busy.

Good to Know

Tavern off the Green is located at 127 Morris Street, Morristown, NJ. Because the open jam runs on a biweekly rather than weekly cadence, it is worth checking the venue's current live-music calendar before heading over.

title: Laundromat Speakeasy
venue_description:
Laundromat Speakeasy

Hidden below street level in downtown Morristown, Laundromat Speakeasy is a 23-and-over cocktail bar built around a hidden-in-plain-sight speakeasy concept, occupying the basement space that once held the long-running Dark Horse Lounge. The room trades a sports-bar feel for craft cocktails and a curated live entertainment calendar.

Atmosphere and Setting

Exposed brick, low light and an intimate basement footprint set the tone: this is a cocktail-forward room built for listening and mingling rather than a big stage production. The regular booking calendar leans local and regional acts across genres.

Live Music and the Wednesday Jam

The venue's own published live-entertainment schedule lists a Jam Session running Wednesdays from 7:00 PM to close. Thursday through Saturday it runs a fuller live-band schedule spanning blues, funk and rock acts. A note for visitors: the venue's general hours page separately lists Monday through Wednesday as closed, so the Wednesday jam may have shifted since it was last posted — it is worth confirming the current week's schedule directly with the venue by phone or social media before making a special trip.

Other Events

Beyond the Wednesday jam, Laundromat Speakeasy runs a steady Thursday-through-Saturday live-music lineup alongside its full cocktail program.

Good to Know

Laundromat Speakeasy is located at 4 DeHart Street (basement level), Morristown, NJ. As a 23-and-over venue, valid ID is required for entry.

title: Morristown Unitarian Universalist Fellowship
venue_description:
Morristown Unitarian Universalist Fellowship — Home of The Folk Project's Open Stage

Once a month, the fellowship hall at the Morristown Unitarian Universalist Fellowship becomes one of the area's most established listening rooms for acoustic and folk performers, hosting The Folk Project's long-running Open Stage series.

Atmosphere and Setting

This is not a bar-room jam. The Folk Project runs a smoke-free, alcohol-free listening-room environment on a proper concert stage that seats roughly 200, with a second, smaller Terrace Room stage also available the same night. The tone is attentive and community-minded, closer to a folk club or house concert than a nightlife venue.

The Open Stage

Billed by the organization as "North Jersey's premier open stage," the event runs on the second Friday of each month at 7:30 PM, with $7 admission (children 12 and under free with an adult). Unlike a walk-in open mic, performers request a slot in advance by email; up to 15 acts are selected for two-song ten-minute sets. Performers can opt for accompaniment from the house Bunk Bed Band, and sets are livestreamed and recorded for the artists. The format leans acoustic, singer-songwriter and folk.

Other Programming

The Folk Project also runs the Troubadour Acoustic Concert Series and occasional ticketed shows such as Campfire Night at the Troubadour out of the same space, making the fellowship hall a hub for the area's acoustic and folk community well beyond the monthly open stage.

Good to Know

The fellowship uses the mailing address 21 Normandy Heights Road, Morristown, NJ; the facility sits near the Morristown/Morris Township line. Because the open stage is application-based rather than walk-in, performers should reach out to The Folk Project in advance through its website rather than showing up expecting a same-night slot.
